Dakar Girls

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its a race very few would dare take on , but two South African women are braving the elements to take on the toughest motorbike race - the Dakar rally

Unique Selling Point:
This year the off-road endurance race will feature two South African women: Taye Perry and Kistren Landman, they join 12 other women from around the world who will be competing in this year's Dakar. The pair will be the first South African women to compete in the Dakar.

Kirsten Landman:
Kirsten Landman’s journey to the Dakar maybe really started in Botswana after a terrible crash that put her in a coma for 11 days. After recovering, she knew she would never again compete in an off-road rally. A conversation with Joey Evans who finished the Dakar in 2017 despite being partly paraplegic started making her think. What was first an idea before turned to a goal. Kirsten is one of the best hard enduro riders of South-Africa will be on the start line of her first Dakar. On her bike she had her mottos written on her handlebars: “keep wheels turning” on the left, “get to the finish line” on the right, to hoepfully become the first African lady to complete the Dakar on a bike.

Taye Perry:
she battle it out with Kirsten to become the first African woman to finish the Dakar on a bike, she’ll also be one of the smallest competitors in the history of the Dakar. But the fact she’s 1m58 certainly isn’t a concern for her, she started riding bikes from the age of 12. She had learn to adapt to the big KTM 450 rally bike and turned a few heads with her fearless style of riding .

Press Release:


The Dakar Girls
The Dakar rally is an endurance race like no other – 7900 KM in twelve gruelling days across the harshest terrain Saudi Arabia has to offer. It’s a race that the pushes riders to their limits – the ultimate challenge that very few would dare take on, but this year two South African women took their place amongst some of the most elite racers in world. One is known as “The iron lady of hard ‘enduro’”, and the other, “The Desert Rose”. Carte Blanche meets these two extraordinary riders who beat the odds and returned as conquering heroes.
Producer: Sinethemba Nogude | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


Dakar Ladies
Opening Sequence ( 26 seconds)
Link Derek: The Dakar rally is one of the toughest events on earth over the years thirty competitors have died 21 of them on motorbikes.
V/O : It's a dangerous challenge very few would dare take on, but this year two South African women set out to conquer this epic race in what would be 12 days of racing across the most unforgiving terrain in Saudi Arabia.
V/O As Kirsten Landman and Taye Perry lined up against the best in the world this would be the ultimate test of their endurance and spirit.
Taye Perry Upsound: 05:01 I was very nervous, when the officials came to me and said this a point of no return- once you go over this podium, its over, it’s the beginning but its over ,
Upsound : Kirsten Landman : I grew up watching Dakars and you see all these guys crying exhausted they cant get out of a section , It is so physically tough and draining.
V/O Kirsten’s love for motorbike racing began at the tender the age of 8, when a friendly bet with her father Mario turned into a lifetime passion.
UpSound : It started at a young age, I remember sticking a poster in my wall and said dad I want a motorbike.
Upsound Mario:00:19 when she came to me with the bike story, I said to her over my dead body but she kept hounding me and I said ok I will make a deal with you-if you get into the Gauteng team and you have got a bike
V/O: And she did
Upsound: When I left school I was picked up by Bidvest Yamaha team and then KTM// not many can say they turned their path to their profession AND I DID
VO For Taye motorsport was in her DNA.
Upsound Hein : My kids were growing up and we started going through photgraphs at the army and bikes and stuff , Taye found photographs of my old 200 R, popping wheelies and showing off in the old days and when she saw that she wanted to know where this was coming from, and that was the catch on.
Upsound Taye My dad has always been my riding buddy for my whole riding career and I think we’ve worked on each other and we’ve built our skills together .Nothing makes me feel more alive , racing is what I love,its my passion
Derek Link : Imagine riding a bike for over two weeks covering thousands of kilometers and your feet dont even touch the ground, at 1,58 meters around 5 feet 2 , thats the courage of Taye Perry.
Upsoudn Taye Perry : I am very safe when I am at speedI never crash when I am going fast, its only when I am slow, when I need to put the leg down then its not there, that is when I am down, usually for second gear stuff and tight sections, its been a long road , even right until i was at Dakar ,it wasnt at all certain because finding dunds and all that doesn't stop.
V/OBut for Kirsten Landman the path to Dakar was complex.
Link Derek Ironically it was an absolutely horrific crash during a race in Botswana what would set Kirsten on her road to Dakar.
Upsound Mario:I got a call one night to say your daughter has been involved in this crash and it took my breath away.
Upsound: Kirsten Landman: What had happened was I severed my pancreas off my small intestine and all that fluid in my intestine had leaked all over my abdomin and I started vomiting up this back stuff,every organ went septic , I was put into an induced coma for 11 days ,I was put onto life support because I was on morphine , my heart stopped. I swore after that to never ever ride off riding again. Someone said to me in an interview what about the dakar Rally , I said to him bud thank you but no thank you to do tha Dakar rally.
V/O After a speedy recovery her friend and Dakar hero Joey Evans was there to give her a push.
Upsound Joey Evans: I said to her you’ve gotta to that race and she is a bit scared of the fast stuff and before lond she started to ask the question : tell me about this ,Tell me about this , you could see the seed is starting to grow , she was like alright I am going to do this.
V/O After months of hard work and Preparation, it was time to race - It was rider and machine versus the elements and after a few punishing stages and the fatal crash of top rider Paulo Goncalves Kirsten and Taye were charging ahead.
Upsound: Dunes , I expected more sand ,but it was very rocky // I wanted to face my fears and do it in the biggest hardest fastest race in the world and that was the Dakar Rally.// It was also high speed were split seconds mean a lot you’ve got to stay focussed //Everyday is a new adventure you have no idea what lies ahead of you.

V/O Taye had a commanding lead in the race to be the first African woman on a motorbike to finish the Dakar ,but Kirsten was hot on her track
Upsound Derek: Going into the penultimate stage you were looking good, top 50 overrall, what happened on that second last stage?
Upsound Taye Perry: It started really well , It had rained days before so we were loving life in the dunes and then I had one or two falls in the sand and the third fall which was around 200 during the special and my bike wont start it just swung , I was crying and I was praying and it was so hard to deal with, I was basically on that edge where I had expected that my Dakar is over and then the guys who rescued me basically , they stopped there and said this is not the end of your dakar , we are going to help you, they towed me the rest of the way , it was the longest afternoon and evening of my life, I couldnt believe I was still in the race.It was not registering.
V/O Perry’s loss was Landmans gain , she powered to 55th place overrall and Third among the women to become the first woman from africa on a motorbike to finish Dakar...Taye Perry would finish 77th overrall and 4th among the women.
Upsound kirsten : It was like it was meant to be the first african woman to finish the Dakar , over the moon with Joy and I’ve got a very supportive family and I wouldnt be here , done what I had done , I wouldnt have been in a motorbike if they didnt support me
Upsound Joey Evan : No woman from Africa have ever finished in the bike category before , it is not something youve got to take on lightely and it is also something that you can wing it, its a case that you have to ride that bike and I think that people like Kirsten and Taye are , I think that there is something deep down in them that is a bit superhuman.

• The Dakar is a race that pushes riders to the limit – thousands of kilometres across unforgiving terrain , Meet the two South African women who beat the odds and returned as heroes.

• One is “The iron lady of hard Enduro”, whilst the other “The Desert Rose” ,we meet the two South Africa women who beat the odds and conquered the Dakar Rally.

• The Dakar rally is an endurance race like no other – thousands of Kilometers across the harshest terrain , How did Taye Perry and Kirsten Landman conquer this epic race?
